problem: Given a cylinder, find the differential $\text{d}V$ for the volume $V$ of the cylinder if the radius is $r=2$ and the height is $h=4.$
worked_solution:
The volume of the cylinder is $V=\pi {r}^{2}h.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(r,h) & =(\frac{∂V}{∂r})\,\text{d}r+(\frac{∂V}{∂h})\,\text{d}h \\  & =2\pi rh\,\text{d}r+\pi {r}^{2}\,\text{d}h\end{aligned}
$$

For $r=2$ and $h=4,$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(2,4) & =2\pi \cdot 2\cdot 4\,\text{d}r+\pi \cdot {2}^{2}\,\text{d}h \\  & =16\pi \,\text{d}r+4\pi \,\text{d}h.\end{aligned}
$$
